theater: 上努比亞第二瀑布前線

battle.name: 圖特摩斯二世的行動
battle.theater: 上努比亞第二瀑布前線
battle.brief: 前1493年，埃及第十八王朝第二王圖特摩斯二世即位，庫什等外邦趁換王反叛。他未親征，改遣父遺老將鎮壓上努比亞肯特亨諾費爾之亂，另分兵沿西奈走廊討沙蘇貝都因人，並遠入上黎凡特至「尼」地。卡面的埃及月牙劍，正是遠征軍車陣衝鋒後近身纏鬥的副兵器。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 此役的交戰方，是埃及新王國第十八王朝與其境外的北方與南方外邦。埃及方面以王座為最高發令處，軍令經王室書吏與將軍一級的軍官分發，實戰編制以車隊為骨，步兵按上埃及、下埃及與三角洲守軍分屬各支隊，後勤由神官兼軍需官的體系與尼羅河船隊承擔；南方前線是圖特摩斯一世修築的要塞梯形線——象島、賽尼特、塞姆納、布能——各段由守備官率兵駐守，另有巡邏隊沿河與沿沙漠線巡邏。北方的對手沒有統一國家：西奈沙漠的沙蘇貝都因人以劫掠邊境與商路為生，上黎凡特一帶（敘利亞與黎巴嫩山地）則由數名互不隸屬的弓首領各自引兵，任何一方都沒有遠程砲術、攻城器械或可支撐長期圍城的糧秣。整場行動本質是一次以鎮壓為主、掠奪為輔的邊疆戰，而不是兩國之間的會戰。
countriesEn: The parties in this action were the Egyptian New Kingdom of the Eighteenth Dynasty and the foreign lands to its north and south. On the Egyptian side the throne was the supreme source of orders; commands went out through the royal scribes and the officials who held the title of general, and the tactical order of battle rested on the chariot corps, with infantry drawn from Upper Egypt, Lower Egypt and the Delta garrisons. Supply was in the hands of the priest-administrator system and of the Nile fleet. The southern front was the stepped line of forts left by Thutmose I — Elephantine, Semna, Buhen — each sector manned by a garrison commander, with patrols working the river and the desert tracks. The opponents in the north had no state at all: the Shasu Bedouins of the Sinai desert lived on raiding the frontier and the caravan roads, while in Upper Retenu, in Syria and the Lebanon highlands, a number of unrelated bows, the local chieftain titles, each led his own men. Neither of them possessed artillery, siege engines or the foodstuffs needed to sustain a long siege. In its essence this was a frontier war of suppression with a little plunder on the side, not a set-piece battle between two states.
people: 圖特摩斯二世（Djehutymes，第十八王朝第四位法老，圖特摩斯一世與王后穆特諾弗雷特之子）是這場行動的發動者，但他即位時年紀尚輕，多數學者認為只有十幾歲，因此並未像父親那樣親領大軍：南線的鎮壓由圖特摩斯一世留下的老將指揮，北線的討伐也交給部將與書吏軍官。留下文字記錄者是皇家書吏兼上埃及軍隊統帥阿摩斯·彭·奈赫貝特，他在埃爾卡布的墓誌中自述奉命討伐沙蘇貝都因人，這段記載被後世視為埃及人與沙蘇在沙漠直接交手的證據。軍中還有象島與塞姆納的守備官、工程官伊奈尼（Ineni，其自傳跨越圖特摩斯二世全朝，並記下宮殿工程），以及後來在圖特摩斯三世朝出任高級大官的雷克米爾。對面陣營的領袖多無姓名流傳：阿斯旺碑只記下庫什北方的首長與兩名庫施首長之子率眾起事，所領部眾被碑文說成外地分成五部。希臘化時代的約瑟夫斯在《駁阿庇翁》中把這段北方動線稱為埃塞俄比亞戰爭，那是歐洲傳統對這場行動唯一的名稱。
peopleEn: Thutmose II (Djehutymes, fourth pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty, son of Thutmose I and the queen Mutnofret) set the action in motion, but he was very young at his accession and most scholars put him in his teens, so he did not lead a great army in person as his father had. The suppression in the south was carried out by the veteran generals inherited from Thutmose I, and the northern raid was delegated to departmental commanders and scribe-officers. The man who put it on record was the royal scribe and commander of the Upper Egyptian troops Ahmose Pen-Nekhbet, whose tomb at el-Kab states that he was sent against the Shasu Bedouins, and that passage is treated as the direct trace of Egyptian contact with the Shasu in the desert. Around him in the command were the garrison commanders of Elephantine and Semna, the architect Ineni, whose autobiography spans the whole reign of Thutmose II and records the palace works, and Rekhmire, who later held the highest administrative office under Thutmose III. Few of the enemy leaders are named: the Aswan stela records only a chief to the north of Kush and two sons of the chief of Kush raising the tribes, leading a population that the text says was divided into five parts. In the Hellenistic age Josephus, in Against Apion, called this phase the Ethiopic War, and that is the only name the European tradition ever gave the operation.
kits: 卡面這件埃及月牙劍（Khopesh）在戰役體系裡是副兵器，不是主力。第十八王朝的埃及兵在遠征中以複合反曲弓作主要殺傷手段，配長矛、短矛與窄刃戰斧：斧負責砍伐與破障，矛負責中距離刺穿，月牙劍則專門處理兩種時刻——車陣衝鋒之後、雙方貼身糾纏的短兵相接，以及清剿潰散之眾與爭奪敵方戰車。它是單刃、外彎、刃口開在內弧、尖端漸收的短柄彎刀，銅合金刀身安在木柄上再以皮帶纏握，砍下去可以拖著走而不用拔出來，適合在狹窄的村落街道與車陣縫隙中揮動，因此常配給王族侍衛、車隊護衛與專職近戰的步兵。同一場行動裡真正支撐遠征的裝備還有：雙輪輕戰車（單匹馬拉動，車上三人：御者、持矛或弓的車長、持斧或劍的護兵）、駱駝隊（在西奈與黎凡特一線運送水囊、麵粉與椰棗）、尼羅河船隊（把穀物運到賽尼特與塞姆納的倉廩，並把戰車與馬匹送上陸路），以及沿途要點的儲糧與皮革水袋。這一役沒有攻城戰記載，因此也不見攻城塔、破城槌或任何攻城器投入。
kitsEn: The Egyptian khopesh on the card is a side arm in this order of battle, not a main weapon. On the Egyptian campaigns of the Eighteenth Dynasty the composite reflex bow did most of the killing, supported by the long spear, the short spear and the narrow-bladed battle axe: the axe for hacking and for breaking through obstacles, the spear for reaching out at middle distance, and the khopesh for the two moments that decided a close fight, namely the confusion after a chariot charge when men came to grips, and the mopping up of broken formations and the seizing of enemy chariots. It is a single-edged, outward-curved blade with the cutting edge on the inner arc and a point that tapers away, a short-hafted scimitar of copper alloy with a wooden grip bound in leather; it can be cut and drawn along without having to be pulled back, which suits the narrow streets of a village or the gaps between chariots, so it was normally carried by the royal guard, by chariot crews and by infantry detailed for close fighting. The equipment that actually sustained the march was otherwise: light two-wheel chariots drawn by a single horse and crewed by three, a driver, a spearman or archer, and an axeman or swordsman; camel trains carrying water skins, flour and dates across Sinai and the Levant; the Nile fleet moving grain to the magazines at Semna and Buhen and delivering horses and chariots to the land route; and the stored grain and leather waterskins at the depots along the line. There is no record of any siege in this action, and no siege tower, battering ram or other siege engine was committed to it.
tactics: 這次行動的基本結構是一南一北、兩路同時壓制。南線沿尼羅河逆流而上，依托圖特摩斯一世留下的梯形要塞線逐段推進：先穩住第二瀑布的塞姆納與布能，再把巡邏隊推向庫什方向；遠征主力不越過能穩定供水的極限，因為一旦離開河道與倉廩，後勤就會斷。北線則沿海之路，即西奈北端的沿海商道推進，先掃平沙蘇的游擊，再向黎凡特山地深入。作戰時車隊集中使用，作為衝鋒、突破與追擊的工具；步兵分列兩翼，以弓矢覆蓋接近路線，車隊破門或擾亂之後，步兵以矛、斧與月牙劍收拾近身戰。埃及軍的慣例是遠征只在涼季進行，即洪水季之後到酷暑之前，回程必須趕在夏天以前；因此這場北方掠奪戰即使深入到尼地，也會在水與草料耗盡時折返，不會就地設防。沙漠與山地都利於游擊而非會戰，埃及人沒有像對付近東城邦那樣使用圍城或大型攻城器，也沒有在敵境建立永久的行政機構。
tacticsEn: The basic shape of the operation was two simultaneous suppressions, one to the south and one to the north. The southern column moved up the Nile against the current, leaning on the stepped fort line left by Thutmose I and pushing forward section by section: secure Semna and Buhen at the second cataract first, then drive the patrols towards Kush. The marching body did not go beyond the limit of secure water, because once the column left the river and the magazines, supply broke down. The northern column used the coastal road through northern Sinai, the Way of the Sea, sweeping away the Shasu raids before pushing into the Levantine highlands. In action the chariots were concentrated as the instrument of charge, breakthrough and pursuit; infantry went on the flanks, archers covering the approaches with volleys, and after the chariots had broken the enemy or the gates the infantry finished the close work with spear, axe and khopesh. Egyptian custom was to campaign in the cool season only, that is after the inundation and before the worst heat, and the return march had to beat the summer; so the northern raid turned back when water and fodder ran out even when it reached the place called Niy, and it left no garrison behind. Both the desert and the hill country favoured skirmishers over pitched battle, and the Egyptians used neither circumvallation nor great siege works against the towns of the Near East, nor did they set up any permanent administration in enemy territory.
data: 年表方面，低年表把圖特摩斯二世的在位定為前1493至前1479年，另有學者主張他只統治三年，約前1482至前1479年，本條按所採年表記為前1493年。現存最高年號見證是阿斯旺碑，紀年為在位第一年、第一洪水季第二月第八日，內容記載庫什謀反、掠奪發生在圖特摩斯一世修築的防線之後，以及外地被分成五部。距離方面，從阿斯旺到第二瀑布的塞姆納與布能前線，順尼羅河而上約三百公里；從埃及東北部邊界到上黎凡特的尼地約六百至七百公里；到幼發拉底河自東北邊界算約八百公里，自底比斯算則超過一千二百公里，那裡是圖特摩斯一世曾越過的界標。兵力方面，圖特摩斯二世的殘篇沒有留下任何數字；同一王朝的遠征通常包含數百輛戰車與相應的步兵及輜重人員，總人數當以萬計，但這是依編制所作的推估，不能當作確數。史料密度上，圖特摩斯二世存世的聖甲蟲印章數量遠少於圖特摩斯一世與哈特謝普蘇特，碑刻與自傳也大量被後人改刻，這正是這場行動細節稀少的原因。
dataEn: On the chronology: the low chronology places the reign of Thutmose II from 1493 to 1479 BC, while other scholars argue that he ruled only three years, roughly 1482 to 1479 BC; this entry follows the former and dates the action to 1493 BC. The highest dated attestation of the king is the Aswan stela, dated to Year 1, second month of the first inundation season, day 8; it recounts the conspiracy of Kush, the plunder taken behind the fortification lines built by Thutmose I, and the statement that the foreign lands were divided into five parts. For distances: the Nile run from Aswan to the Semna and Buhen front at the second cataract is about three hundred kilometres; from Egypt's north-eastern frontier to the place called Niy in Upper Retenu is roughly six to seven hundred kilometres; and the Euphrates lies about eight hundred kilometres beyond the north-eastern frontier, or more than twelve hundred from Thebes, the river Thutmose I had already crossed. On numbers of men: the fragmentary annals of Thutmose II preserve no figure at all. Campaigns of this dynasty normally carried several hundred chariots with the infantry and baggage train to match, so a host of thousands of men is implied, but that is an inference from the order of battle and not a figure recorded for this king. On the thinness of the record: the number of Thutmose II's scarabs known to survive is far below those of Thutmose I or Hatshepsut, and his inscriptions and autobiographies were largely re-cut under later kings, which is precisely why the details of this action are so few.
cause: 直接起因是王位更替帶來的邊疆鬆動。圖特摩斯一世死後，圖特摩斯二世於前1493年即位，阿斯旺碑開篇即寫庫什開始謀反，讓兩地之主的臣民萌生叛念，說明庫什與北方部族在埃及換王時的慣例是趁亂反攻。內部原因是新王年幼：中央對南線要塞與西奈邊境的控制一度鬆手，埃及守軍退守圖特摩斯一世修的堡壘，讓反叛者得以在其後方劫掠。外部原因是北方的聯防態勢：沙蘇部族年年入掠西奈與邊境商路，埃及商隊與紅海貿易受威脅；上黎凡特一帶的弓首領在埃及插手河套的形勢下聯合抵抗，維持對黎凡特的獨佔。北線遠征因此不只是懲罰游擊，更是要把圖特摩斯一世越過幼發拉底河建立的聲望確認一次——圖特摩斯一世曾在尼地獵象，那裡是前代遠征的極限標記，新王必須證明那條線仍然有效。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the loosening of the frontier that a change of ruler always brought. Thutmose I died, Thutmose II took the throne in 1493 BC, and the Aswan stela opens with the words that Kush began to conspire, making the subjects of the lord of the Two Lands consider revolt; Kush and the northern tribes took advantage of the accession as they customarily did. The internal cause was the youth of the new king. Control of the southern forts and of the Sinai border slipped, the Egyptian garrisons fell back into the strongholds Thutmose I had built, and the rebels were able to plunder behind the lines. The external cause was the defensive alliance in the north. The Shasu came down year after year on Sinai and the frontier caravan roads, threatening Egyptian traders and the Red Sea commerce, while the bows of Upper Retenu united to resist Egyptian interference in the Euphrates valley and to keep the Levant to themselves. The northern raid was therefore not merely a punishment for raiding: it was a statement that the prestige his father had built by crossing the Euphrates still held, since Thutmose I had hunted elephants at Niy, the marker of the limit of the earlier march, and the new king had to show that the line still worked.
impact: 這場行動沒有改變任何一條國界，卻為後來十餘年的埃及北進定下路線。南線上，庫什叛亂被壓回第二瀑布以北，埃及在塞姆納與布能的守備恢復正常，但沒有再深入；北線上，埃及軍隊第一次在圖特摩斯二世時代打通西奈走廊、加利利到奧龍特斯河上游這條進入黎凡特的線，十二年後他的兒子圖特摩斯三世沿著同一條路打到美吉多、幼發拉底河乃至更北的敘利亞內陸，這一役等於那次大規模西征的先導與偵察。制度上，它確立了新王不必親征、由王室將領與書吏軍官代為執行遠征的運作方式，並留下工程官的自傳同時記錄宮殿工程與邊疆戰事這種把國家工程與戰役綁在一起的記錄方式。此外，圖特摩斯二世在位期間，王后哈特謝普蘇特已主持紅海瓦迪加瓦西斯遠征的籌備，並在卡納克興工；幾年後她自行加冕為王，說明這場邊疆行動發生的年代，權力中樞其實已有另一個核心在運作，這也影響了後來埃及對北方戰線的部署節奏。
impactEn: The action changed no border, but it fixed the road that Egypt would take north for the next dozen years. In the south the revolt of Kush was pushed back above the second cataract, the Egyptian garrison at Semna and Buhen returned to normal, and there was no advance beyond it. In the north the Egyptian army, under Thutmose II, for the first time opened the line from the Sinai corridor and Galilee to the upper Orontes into the Levant; twelve years later his son Thutmose III marched the same road to Megiddo, to the Euphrates and deeper into Syria, so this operation was the advance guard and reconnaissance of that greater campaign. Institutionally it established the practice that a new king need not campaign in person and that royal commanders and scribe-officers would carry out long expeditions on his behalf, and it left behind the kind of record in which an architect's autobiography ties palace building to frontier war. There was something else: while this action was being fought, the queen Hatshepsut was already preparing the Red Sea expedition from Wadi Gawasis and had begun work at Karnak; a few years later she crowned herself king. The power centre of the period already had a second core, and that fact shaped the way the Egyptian war effort in the north was later paced.
result: 結果是兩線皆平、寸土未得。南線方面，庫什的叛軍被埃及軍迅速壓回，前線退回第二瀑布的塞姆納與布能一線，阿斯旺碑記下的是一場成功的鎮壓，而不是一次征服；叛軍首領被拘，其勢力退回庫什北界，軍隊沒有越過第二瀑布深入，也沒有在南方建立新的駐軍或行政機構。北線方面，沙蘇部族被打散，數名首領被帶回埃及；掠奪性的遠征深入上黎凡特到尼地一帶，卻因水與草料到頂而折返，既沒有攻下城池，也沒有留下駐軍或界碑，幼發拉底河彼岸那塊著名的界碑仍屬於他的父親圖特摩斯一世。損失主要來自行軍而非攻城：傷亡出在沙蘇游擊、酷熱與缺水，縱隊為水源與草料必須壓縮，戰車與馬匹的損耗由後方船隊補給。最後是戰術上的收穫：埃及人把車隊衝鋒、弓兵覆蓋、斧矛近戰加月牙劍收尾這套組合帶進了後來對米坦尼與敘利亞的戰爭，而真正把埃及軍推過幼發拉底河的，是他的兒子圖特摩斯三世。
resultEn: The result was that both lines held and no ground was gained. In the south the Kush rebels were driven back quickly, the front returned to the Semna and Buhen line at the second cataract, and the Aswan stela records a successful suppression rather than a conquest; the rebel chiefs were taken and their strength retreated to the northern frontier of Kush. No army went below the second cataract, and no new garrison or administrative office was created in the south. In the north the Shasu were scattered and several of their chiefs were brought back to Egypt; the raid reached Niy in Upper Retenu and then turned back when water and fodder ran out. No city was taken, no garrison and no boundary stone were left behind, and the famous stele on the far side of the Euphrates still belonged to his father Thutmose I. The losses were those of a march rather than of a siege: they came from Shasu skirmishers, from heat and shortage of water, the column had to be compressed to keep up with the water and fodder, and horses and chariots were made good from the fleet behind it. The lasting result was tactical. Egypt carried the combination of chariot charge, screened archers, axe-and-spear close work and the khopesh to finish it into the later wars against Mitanni and Syria, but it was Thutmose III, his son, who finally pushed the Egyptian army across the Euphrates.
